title: Event-coalescer rewrite for observability ingestion and non-blocking exporter adapter
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Background: Our current observability ingestion pipeline serializes and forwards each span/metric/log event synchronously to exporters. Under load this causes high tail latencies, export backpressure, and elevated CPU due to serialization hot paths. Goal: Replace the synchronous forwarder with an event-coalescer + non-blocking exporter adapter that batches related events, applies a lightweight eviction policy for stale KV cache traces, and offers a zero-copy encoding fast-path for the most common span shapes. This ticket scopes the core runtime refactor, a lightweight API shim for legacy exporters, and a plan for an incremental rollout with canary metrics.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end ingestion path switches to coalescer without increase in dropped telemetry vs baseline
P50 tokenized export latency <= baseline and P99 tail latency reduced by >= 35% under 95th percentile load profile
CPU usage of runtime observability hotpath reduced by >= 15% in synthetic load tests
No increase in span/metric cardinality in production sampling buckets; sampling behaviour preserves previous guarantees
All existing exporters continue to function via the exporter-adapter shim with feature flag off for fallback
Rolling canary completed with automated rollback on error budget breach
tasks: Design: finalize event-coalescer data model and eviction rules (Confluence link in attachments)
Implement coalescer ring buffers and non-blocking handoff to exporter workers
Introduce zero-copy proto/json encoder for common span schema and integrate into hotpath
Build exporter-adapter shim that provides backward compatibility for sync exporters
Add feature flag gating and per-tenant opt-in for initial canary
Integration tests and end-to-end perf harness for span/metric/log workloads
Create rollout playbook and alerting dashboard cards for canary monitoring
Post-rollout observability audit and cleanup of deprecated sync-forwarder code
risk: Eviction policy mistakes could surface incomplete traces to downstream systems; exporter-adapter bugs could increase dropped telemetry. Will mitigate via canary, test harness and shadow mode for 48h before enabling persistent batching.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag and run QA in staging with high-fidelity replay
Enable on 3 internal tenants (low traffic) for 24h in shadow mode (no exporter writes), compare outputs
Canary: enable batching+coalescer for 5% of production traffic for 6 hours; monitor error budget, dropped spans, P99 export latency
If stable, expand to 25% for 24 hours, then 100% across non-critical regions
Final step: migrate critical regions after 72h with per-region rollback controls

This change intentionally avoids touching the public SDK surface; SDKs remain unchanged. Only runtime ingestion path is modified.
